summary: Dispatch, run-status, coordination preflight, and runtime-blocker-taxonomy tools.

tools.notes: MCP-only agent role dispatch for worker, reviewer, and redteam. The normal call supplies only role and subject. On every dispatch the launcher reads the role model from repo-root agent-launch.toml and derives app/backend through the neutral model registry; typed app/model are explicit per-dispatch overrides only. Missing, malformed, or unknown role configuration refuses actionably with no family fallback. Same-user stdio MCP is not an authentication boundary; the real boundary is the launcher sandbox plus work-record admission. Caller-supplied identity carriers (request payload, prompt text, ambient env, argv, claimed_identity.role) are refused and never become selection authority. Worker and reviewer accept a WK or slice; redteam also accepts an IN. Non-dispatchable subjects refuse with work_record_readiness_failure. A reviewer subject with non-empty write_scope refuses with role_policy_violation / reviewer_write_scope_nonempty; remediate with a separate findings-only review unit, not a role change or readiness bypass. Refusals use stable runtime-blocker taxonomy codes. Route worker/reviewer/redteam dispatch through this MCP tool only; if the launch backend is unconfigured, report the blocker rather than falling back to wrappers, shell, env, or bwrap changes.
use_when: The dispatch_role_call intent has a dispatchable workspace_validate_dispatch result for the same unit and role.
do_not_use_when: Readiness is unknown; use workspace_validate_dispatch first.
The task asks about an existing run; use workspace_agent_run_status or workspace_agent_run_wait.
requires_prior_state: Same-unit same-role workspace_validate_dispatch result with dispatchable=true.

paid_cce.notes: MCP-only agent role dispatch for worker, reviewer, and redteam. The normal call supplies only role and subject. On every dispatch the launcher reads the role model from repo-root agent-launch.toml and derives app/backend through the neutral model registry; typed app/model are explicit per-dispatch overrides only. Missing, malformed, or unknown role configuration refuses actionably with no family fallback. Same-user stdio MCP is not an authentication boundary; the real boundary is the launcher sandbox plus work-record admission. Caller-supplied identity carriers (request payload, prompt text, ambient env, argv, claimed_identity.role) are refused and never become selection authority. Worker and reviewer accept a WK or slice; redteam also accepts an IN. Non-dispatchable subjects refuse with work_record_readiness_failure. A reviewer subject with non-empty write_scope refuses with role_policy_violation / reviewer_write_scope_nonempty; remediate with a separate findings-only review unit. Refusals use stable runtime-blocker taxonomy codes. When CCE/Node Engine refusal output includes a valid worker_admission.recovery.v1 object, treat it as the primary recovery projection: pack_result.recovery is current-decision recovery, while top-level route-problem recovery applies before a pack_result exists. Both are advisory, non-authorizing, resubmission-only guidance; they do not satisfy review evidence, accepted authority, launcher policy, or admission. Legacy reason-fact recovery is compatibility-only when no valid recovery object is present. Malformed, unknown-version, unknown-field, or projection-mismatched recovery fails closed: preserve the underlying refusal, report bounded recovery-contract mismatch guidance, resubmit through CCE, and do not infer local admission, hidden controls, bypasses, or synthesized authorities. Route worker/reviewer/redteam dispatch through this MCP tool only; if the launch backend is unconfigured, report the blocker rather than falling back to wrappers, shell, env, or bwrap changes.

tools.notes: Monitor-handle status query for workspace_agent_dispatch. Caller-supplied identity carriers are refused before handle lookup. Monitor handles are opaque server-issued tokens scoped to subject and role; subject mismatch, replay, and unknown handles refuse via the monitor_handle_* taxonomy. Reports the run lifecycle vocabulary launching, running, succeeded, failed, or cancelled. With no launch executor configured, every handle resolves to MONITOR_HANDLE_UNKNOWN (status=null) — a stable refusal, not the normal posture. Free/local dispatched reviewer/redteam/worker output is prose-only under DEC-0128, so a terminal success with structured_role_result.valid:false is EXPECTED and is not a failed child run, a failed dispatch, or missing findings; a schema-valid structured role result is a paid/CCE capability enabled only by a canonical paid key. Read-only.
use_when: The run_monitoring intent asks for status, output, failure, or completion of an already dispatched run.
do_not_use_when: The task is a new role launch; use workspace_validate_dispatch first.
No monitor handle is available; ask for it instead of searching, reading records, or relaunching.

tools.notes: Bounded-wait companion to workspace_agent_run_status: waits for a dispatched run to reach a terminal state or until a bounded polling window expires, returning one response per call. Omit timeout_ms for the client-safe 60000 ms default; issue successive bounded waits across turns rather than one long client-blocking wait. timed_out:true is a clean wait-window timeout, not a failed run — retry the wait or call run-status with the same monitor_handle; do not relaunch. Out-of-range or non-integer timeout_ms/poll_interval_ms are refused, never silently clamped. Free/local dispatched reviewer/redteam/worker output is prose-only under DEC-0128, so a terminal success with structured_role_result.valid:false is EXPECTED and is not a failed run, a failed dispatch, or missing findings; a schema-valid structured role result is a paid/CCE capability enabled only by a canonical paid key. Shares identity-carrier refusals, workspace resolution, and the monitor_handle_* taxonomy with run-status. Read-only.
use_when: The run_monitoring intent asks to wait briefly for an already dispatched run to finish.
do_not_use_when: The task is a new role launch; use workspace_validate_dispatch first.
No monitor handle is available; ask for it instead of searching, reading records, or relaunching.

tools.notes: Read-only schema-backed runtime blocker taxonomy: the canonical code catalog, categories, the deterministic degraded-state mapping, and the bootstrap-state subset. Dispatch (workspace_agent_dispatch) and the launcher must select blocker codes from this taxonomy rather than inventing ad hoc strings. reviewer_write_scope_nonempty is a structured reason on role_policy_violation (not a separate code), remediated by a separate findings-only review unit.

Read-only coordinator/orchestrator preflight: reports role, caller/session role, subject, allowed durable write surfaces (docs/, wiki/), the implementation/test edit prohibition, repo/docs/wiki writability, available structured dispatch/validation routes, and active runtime blocker codes. A fully read-only mount surfaces as read_only_mount (filesystem category), not as role policy. Caller-supplied identity carriers are refused; role and caller_session_role are caller-asserted introspection knobs.

Orchestrator/operator-only forge handoff for a completed work record. Reuses the exact accumulated WK tip tree as one deterministic one-parent squash commit, publishes one handoff/wk/IN-XXXX/WK-YYYY branch by create-if-absent compare-and-swap, and creates or recovers one pull request against the launcher-configured landing branch. Input is closed: an optional workspace repo alias plus a canonical WK-#### assigned_unit; a slice address is refused. Repository, remote, landing branch, initiative, refs, SHAs, and credentials all derive host-side from the launcher-owned remote and WK state and can never be supplied by caller, prompt, model, or environment. All Git, gh, and credential execution runs host-side outside bwrap; the token never enters a request, result, argv, remote URL, or log. The WK must be terminal and quiescent, and its persistent ref is re-read before every success; any movement refuses. Existing exact branches and pull requests are recovered, never duplicated or overwritten. The forge and organization own review, approval, checks, branch protection, merge, and merge queues. Missing backend, secret, remote, initiative, or configuration returns a typed refusal.
use_when: A work record is complete and quiescent and its accumulated change must be handed to the forge as one squashed pull request.
do_not_use_when: The work record is still active, or an implementation slice or managed run is still open; finish the lifecycle first.
The task asks to merge, approve, rebase, or update an existing branch; the forge and organization policy own those.
authoritative_for: launcher-owned forge branch creation and pull-request create-or-observe
requires_prior_state: A canonical WK-#### record with a canonical initiative assignment and a terminal, quiescent lifecycle.
Launcher-configured landing branch and a forge credential available host-side to the trusted server.
